questions.q: Why are cross-validation rules needed at all?
options: Because segments are independent by default, so any value in one can combine with any value in another unless something restricts it
Because value sets cannot have more than ten values
Because legal entities require them to register
Because currencies cannot be enabled without them
questions.explain: Segments combine freely by default, which can produce nonsense account combinations; cross-validation rules restrict which combinations are actually valid.

questions.q: What are the two parts every cross-validation rule is built from?
options: A legal entity and a business unit
A condition filter and a validation filter
A primary ledger and a secondary ledger
A reference data set and a determinant
questions.explain: A condition filter identifies which combinations a rule applies to, and a validation filter defines what is actually allowed under that condition.

questions.q: How does a cross-validation combination set differ from a cross-validation rule?
options: A combination set replaces the need for a chart of accounts entirely
They are identical in every respect
A combination set is based on an explicit list of valid combinations across up to five segments, rather than a condition/validation filter pair
A combination set can only be used with reporting currencies
questions.explain: Combination sets list valid child-segment-value combinations directly, which is simpler for a finite list but less scalable than pattern-based rules.

questions.q: What advantage comes from referencing a hierarchy node in a cross-validation rule instead of listing individual values?
options: It disables the rule entirely
It requires converting the chart of accounts to a different structure
The rule becomes impossible to maintain
A new value added under that hierarchy's parent is automatically covered by the rule, with no rule change required
questions.explain: Referencing a hierarchy node means the rule automatically extends to new children added under that parent later, reducing ongoing maintenance.

questions.q: What kind of mistake do well-designed cross-validation rules prevent?
options: Entering an incorrect legal address
Creating nonsense account combinations, such as pairing a Manufacturing cost center with a Finance-only natural account
Choosing the wrong conversion rate type
Opening a period before its calendar is defined
questions.explain: Cross-validation rules exist specifically to block illogical account combinations, like pairing segments that should never go together, before they're ever created on a transaction.
